evidence: Traupman 103: I’m mad at you, tibi suscēnseō

phrases.english: he did nothing for you to be cross about
What are you cross about, my boy?

phrases.latin: Tibi suscēnseō, quod mē nōn exspectāvistī.
phrases.english: I’m cross with you for not waiting for me.

phrases.latin: Nōn potes? Nōlī stomachārī; iterum temptā.
phrases.english: You can’t do it? Don’t get frustrated; try again.

phrases.latin: sī enim stomachābere et molestē ferēs, plūra dīcēmus
phrases.english: if you get annoyed and take it badly, we’ll say more
He’s sulking because he isn’t allowed out.

phrases.latin: dēmittō auriculās, ut inīquae mentis asellus, cum gravius dorsō subiit onus
phrases.english: I let my ears droop, like a sulky donkey when a heavier load has been put on his back

sources: Lewis & Short: stomachor · Lewis & Short: succenseo
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 93, 103.
